newsitem.title: UK: Livestock loss small from Central, E.Europe floods.
newsitem.headline: Livestock loss small from Central, E.Europe floods.

text.p: Floods which devastated areas of central and eastern Europe in the past few weeks have left the region's livestock industry largely unscathed, according to local feed industry and government sources.
And feed demand is likely to be little affected, they said.

Germany's compound feed industry association FFMI said in Bonn on Wednesday it saw no demand falls from livestock evacuation or slaughtering, given that the affected area is quite small and not a centre of meat production.
There would also be no impact on meals and feeds transport from the flooding.

It would be possible to get sheep and beef cattle out of the region under the worst case scenario, the sources in the German state of Brandenburg said. But pigs would have to be transported to slaughter in road vehicles and farmers also feared that poultry may be left behind and killed.

In Poland livestock losses were moderate with just above 2,000 cattle killed, more than 6,000 pigs lost and about 1.1 million chickens drowned in the disaster, the head of the ministry's veterinary department Henryk Maciolek said on Tuesday.

The loss of cattle and swine was limited as many animals were evacuated along with thousands of people, he said. In some regions losses have not been estimated yet and figures might change slightly, Maciolek added.
Poland has an estimated 7.3 million head of cattle, 17 million head of swine and around 37 million chickens.

Although the Czech Republic has suffered the worst floods this century, numbers of livestock lost have been minimal and will have little impact on the livestock industry, according to government figures.
A Czech agriculture ministry statement said 295 cattle out of total of 1.87 million died in floods, along with 2,108 pigs out of 4.08 million and 122,000 out of 27.88 million poultry.
"At present there is an overproduction of beef and pigmeat as well as of milk in the Czech Republic," the ministry said. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
